---
title: "Comparing REQ vintages"
description: "Separate history revisions, forecast revisions and forecast errors."
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Comparing REQ vintages}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

Vintage analysis answers different questions. A history revision compares
two realised values, a forecast revision compares an earlier forecast with
the next comparable vintage, and a forecast error compares a forecast with a
later realisation. `readreq` keeps these operations separate and retains the
release IDs, statuses, horizons, source fields and selection rule in the
result.

The observations below are deliberately small synthetic values. They exercise
the public comparison functions without presenting invented numbers as
official REQ data.

## Build a small synthetic vintage set

```{r synthetic-observations}
library(readreq)

synthetic_observation <- function(status, release_id, release_date, value, hash) {
  data.frame(
    product = "synthetic_req_example",
    release_id = release_id,
    release_date = as.Date(release_date),
    dataset = "synthetic_req_example",
    source_dataset = if (status %in% c("estimate", "historical")) {
      "synthetic_history"
    } else {
      "synthetic_forecast"
    },
    source_asset = if (status %in% c("estimate", "historical")) {
      "historical"
    } else {
      "forecast"
    },
    source_sheet = "Synthetic example",
    table_id = "synthetic_export_value",
    table_title = "Synthetic export value",
    record_role = "canonical",
    geography_type = "country",
    geography = "Australia",
    commodity = "Synthetic commodity",
    concept = "export_value",
    period = "2025-26",
    period_start = as.Date("2025-07-01"),
    period_end = as.Date("2026-06-30"),
    period_basis = "australian_financial_year",
    period_status = status,
    status_source = "synthetic example",
    price_basis = "nominal",
    currency = "AUD",
    unit = "A$m",
    value = value,
    raw_value = as.character(value),
    missing_reason = NA_character_,
    footnote_codes = I(list(character())),
    source_note = "Synthetic vignette data; not official REQ values.",
    series_id = paste0("synthetic_export_value_", status),
    observation_key = paste0("synthetic_export_value_", status, "::2025-26"),
    retrieved_at = as.POSIXct("2026-01-01", tz = "UTC"),
    sha256 = hash,
    parser_version = "synthetic",
    section = "Australia",
    frequency = "annual",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

observations <- rbind(
  synthetic_observation(
    "forecast", "example-forecast-a", "2025-12-19", 100,
    paste(rep("a", 64L), collapse = "")
  ),
  synthetic_observation(
    "forecast", "example-forecast-b", "2026-03-20", 104,
    paste(rep("b", 64L), collapse = "")
  ),
  synthetic_observation(
    "estimate", "example-estimate", "2026-06-26", 110,
    paste(rep("c", 64L), collapse = "")
  ),
  synthetic_observation(
    "historical", "example-history", "2026-09-25", 112,
    paste(rep("d", 64L), collapse = "")
  )
)

observations[, c("release_id", "release_date", "period_status", "value")]
```

## Keep the comparison questions separate

```{r comparisons}
compact <- function(x, columns) {
  x <- x[, columns, drop = FALSE]
  row.names(x) <- NULL
  x
}

history_revision <- req_history_revision(observations)
forecast_revision <- req_forecast_revision(observations)
first_error <- req_forecast_error(observations, realisation = "first")
latest_error <- req_forecast_error(
  observations, realisation = "latest_revised"
)

compact(
  history_revision,
  c("old_release_id", "new_release_id", "status_transition", "absolute_change")
)
compact(
  forecast_revision,
  c("old_release_id", "new_release_id", "status_transition", "absolute_change")
)
compact(
  first_error,
  c("old_release_id", "new_release_id", "comparison", "error")
)
compact(
  latest_error,
  c("old_release_id", "new_release_id", "comparison", "error")
)
```

`realisation = "first"` selects the first later estimate or historical value;
`"latest_revised"` selects the latest later realised value and labels the
operation accordingly. `compare_req_vintages()` is a convenience wrapper when
you want one comparison family from an already parsed multi-vintage data
frame.

```{r wrapper}
compact(
  compare_req_vintages(
    data = observations,
    comparison = "forecast_revision"
  ),
  c("old_release_id", "new_release_id", "comparison", "selection_rule")
)
```

With official data, construct `observations` by reading exact release IDs and
persist the source hashes with the result. `"latest"` is useful for
exploration but is not a stable vintage pin. Comparisons require matching
semantic dimensions (period, unit, currency, price basis, geography and
frequency); non-unique joins fail instead of choosing by row order.
